newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria halts land sales to Topenergy gas firm.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria halts land sales to Topenergy gas firm.

text.p: Bulgaria's public works ministry has ordered two municipalities to halt the sale of land to Bulgarian-Russian gas company Topenergy for the enlargement of a gas pipeline to Turkey, a statement said on Wednesday.
The ministry of regional development and public works said in a statement sales agreed by the municipalities in the northeastern towns of Provadia and Bolyarovo did not meet legal requirements.
The municipalities had not held a tender for the sales, the statement said, adding that it was not clear whether the land concerned was state or municipality property.
"The motives of the decisions (for sale) show an intention to predetermine or hinder a decision of Bulgaria's government about the route and the construction of the pipeline," the statement said.
Topenergy said in May that it was ready to start the construction of a second gas pipeline between the borders of Romania and Turkey for transporting Russian gas to Turkey.
A compressor station for regulating gas volumes will be constructed near Provadia.
Russia's RAO Gazprom, which has a 50 percent stake in Topenergy, is prepared to fund with $30 million the first part of the construction project to be completed by year-end, Topenergy officials said.
Bulgaria's gas monopoly Bulgargas, which represents the interests of the state, holds a 25.1 percent stake in Topenergy but is at odds with the joint firm over transit fees.
The remainder is held by Bulgarian banks and private companies including the powerful Multigroup conglomerate.
Topenergy needs to enlarge the network because annual gas supplies to Turkey are expected to increase from some eight billion cubic metres this year to 12 billion in 2001.
Moscow and Sofia signed in April an intergovernmental agreement on the transit of Russian gas to the Balkans and construction of new pipelines. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
